 First major rain and snowstorms of the season hit Northern California
   Esmeralda Garcia   
Friday, November 13, 2026 
 | Sacramento, CA 
 Cars drive by during a rain storm Friday, Nov. 22, 2024, in Sacramento.
 (Gerardo Zavala/CapRadio)
 Rainy and snowy conditions are coming in strong in the Sacramento region and the Sierra Nevadas as a result of atmospheric rivers .  
 In the valley, heavy rain will continue throughout Friday, with a wind advisory through the evening. Gusts of wind may reach up to 32 mph. Saturday will be drier but rainfall returns on Sunday and may continue into Monday. Drivers should expect slick roads and possible flooding in low areas.  
 In Tahoe, a winter storm warning is in effect from Friday until Saturday morning. Snow is expected to return on Sunday. Traveling is highly discouraged, and drivers should expect chain controls and travel delays.  
 Atmospheric rivers are narrow rivers of moisture in the atmosphere that begin in tropical oceans and carry that moisture towards higher elevations and watersheds. Once it reaches these conditions, the moisture becomes rain or snow.  
 The effects of this atmospheric river are heightened by the current El Niño season, which is predicted to strengthen throughout the winter. According to UCLA’s Neelin Group , a climate research group, an El Niño happens when “the sea surface temperatures (SSTs) in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean are warmer than average.”  
 To ensure safety this wet season, the City of Sacramento asks residents to keep storm drains clear, secure your outdoor items, understand your flood risk and sign up for local weather alerts.
